eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus for San Francisco’s August 20 high centers on 67–70 °F**, reflecting persistent onshore marine flow and a shallow marine layer that limits daytime heating. National Weather Service and private models show partly to mostly cloudy skies with west winds of 10–20 mph, keeping maximum temperatures near or slightly below the August average of ~67 °F. Minor model differences in cloud thickness and the precise timing of any afternoon clearing account for the tight spread among the leading market bins (68–69 °F at 36.5 %, 70–71 °F at 28.5 %, 66–67 °F at 19 %). A cooling trend noted in recent NWS discussions reinforces the expectation of no significant warm-air advection or offshore flow that could push readings into the low 70s or higher. Traders are therefore pricing the outcome almost entirely on the latest model guidance for marine influence and insolation, with resolution hinging on the official NWS high reported for the downtown or airport observation site.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity over Luzon continues to drive elevated cloud cover and scattered rainfall across Metro Manila, moderating daytime heating and keeping maximum temperatures clustered near 31–32°C. PAGASA outlooks valid for August 21 project a 26–32°C range with 40% rain probability, consistent with recent observed highs suppressed below climatological 30–31°C averages by thick cloud decks. Differentiation between the leading 31°C and 32°C outcomes hinges on the exact timing and intensity of convective showers, which can limit peak insolation by 1–2°C; drier breaks or delayed development would favor the higher end. Numerical guidance updates through August 20 and PAGASA’s final morning briefing will refine resolution thresholds ahead of the 24-hour observation window.
